abstract: Cerebrovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Initially insulting the cerebral vasculature, CVD pathology engages the entire neurovascular unit, including endothelial and mural cells, astrocytes, microglia, neurons, and the perivascular fibroblasts and infiltrating peripheral immune cells. Single-cell studies over CVD have generated enormous scattered and heterogeneously annotated atlases, which never supplement an organized visualization and an integrated analysis. Here, we present scCVD (https://scportal.cn/sccvd), an integrated single-cell database of scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data for CVD that characterises expression patterns and chromatin accessibility of CVD-related genes across diverse cell types and disease stages. The current release comprises 701 high-quality samples from four species (human, mouse, rat, and marmoset), encompassing over 4.68 million cells. All datasets were manually curated and standardized, with harmonised metadata covering disease versus control status, disease time points and experimental interventions. scCVD provides analysis modules for differential expression, functional enrichment, trajectory inference, cell-cell communication, transcription factor regulatory networks, and chromatin accessibility, together with interactive visualisation. scCVD also supports convenient data browsing and retrieval, customisable online analysis and batch download, facilitating systematic investigation of cellular heterogeneity and molecular regulatory mechanisms in CVD.
